title: Fewer spreadsheets between the deal team and the answer.

blocks.text: Fewer spreadsheets between the deal team and the answer.

A lean PE team spends its best hours chasing numbers from portfolio companies, reading data rooms and rebuilding the same tracker every quarter. These are the workflows we build to take that work off associates, with a person approving anything that reaches an investment committee.
Portfolio reporting arrives late and in ten formats
Every portfolio company sends its own spreadsheet, on its own schedule. An associate re-keys the figures into the fund template before anyone can compare companies.
Data rooms are read by hand, under a deadline
A data room can hold thousands of files. The first pass is often a person opening contracts to find change-of-control clauses, customer concentration and open litigation.
Sourcing depends on who remembers to look
Target lists are built from a few databases and personal networks. Signals such as a leadership change or a new funding round go unnoticed unless someone happens to see them.
Value creation is a slide, not a backlog
Operating partners know portfolio companies waste time on manual work. Nobody has a ranked list of which processes are worth fixing first.
5 workflows we build for private equity teams
Each workflow below names its trigger, its inputs, what the system is allowed to decide, who signs off and where the result lands. Your stack decides the tools. The pattern stays the same.

What we have shipped that looks like this
These are results from work that uses the same pattern. Most clients are described rather than named.
A construction company (French BTP)
We automated electronic invoicing and subcontractor VAT compliance end to end for a construction business, the kind of back-office process a portfolio audit tends to surface.
Portless (verified reviewer)
We built agents that research a prospect before a call, update the CRM and score leads. The same pattern drives the sourcing workflow above.

One workflow, one owner, a person checking the important decisions. We expand only after the first workflow has a track record.

What should stay human
Deal work carries legal and fiduciary weight. These parts should stay with people.
Investment decisions and valuation judgment
The system can prepare comparables and flag anomalies. It does not decide what a company is worth or whether to bid.
Legal conclusions from contracts
Extraction points a lawyer to the right clause faster. It does not replace legal review of what the clause means for the deal.
Seller and management conversations
Relationship and negotiation stay human. We draft questions and follow-ups, and you decide what to say and when.
Anything an LP or regulator will read
Drafts are labeled as drafts, and a named person approves the final text.
